title: The Messengership Of Prophet Muhammad 16th Degree 2nd Proof The Quran As Decree And Its Miraculousness

questions.question: What is the special message that this person carries?
questions.answer: He carries the Qur’an from Allah.

questions.question: Who accepts this message in every century?
questions.answer: More than 300 million people accept it.

questions.question: How many ways does the passage say this message is amazing?
questions.answer: Seven ways.

questions.question: What book is named for explaining the Qur’an’s miracles in detail?
questions.answer: The Twenty-Fifth Word.

questions.question: About how many sides of miraculousness are mentioned for the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Forty sides.

questions.question: Why does the passage say the traveller does not explain all those proofs here?
questions.answer: Because they are explained in another work.

questions.question: What job does the person have with this message?
questions.answer: He brings it to people and announces it.

questions.question: Why would lying be a very serious wrong for the one who brings this message?
questions.answer: It would go against the message and betray Allah.

questions.question: What does this passage teach us about the truthfulness of the messenger?
questions.answer: He must be truthful and cannot be a liar.

questions.question: What is the main idea of this passage?
questions.answer: The Qur’an is a great miracle, so the one who brings it is trustworthy.

questions.question: In whose hand is the decree said to be?
questions.answer: In the hand of the messenger.

questions.question: Who is the decree from?
questions.answer: It is from the Lord of the universe.

questions.question: What is this decree called?
questions.answer: It is the Qur’an.

questions.question: How do many people respond to this decree over time?
questions.answer: They accept and confirm it century after century.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the Qur’an besides being a decree?
questions.answer: It is wonderful and miraculous.

questions.question: What shows that the Qur’an is not an ordinary book, according to the passage?
questions.answer: It has many miraculous signs.

questions.question: Why is another treatise mentioned in the passage?
questions.answer: It gives strong proofs about the Qur’an’s miraculous nature.

questions.question: What does the traveller conclude about the one who delivers the decree?
questions.answer: He cannot be lying.

questions.question: If that person lied, whom would he wrong?
questions.answer: He would wrong Allah, Who sent the decree.

questions.question: What connection does the passage make between the Qur’an and the messenger’s honesty?
questions.answer: Bringing Allah’s message shows he must be honest.

questions.question: What kind of writing is the Qur’an called in this passage?
questions.answer: It is called a decree.

questions.question: Who sent this decree?
questions.answer: The Creator and Lord of everything sent it.

questions.question: How long has this decree been accepted by huge numbers of people?
questions.answer: Through every century.

questions.question: What number is given for the people who accept it?
questions.answer: More than 300 million people.

questions.question: How many kinds of wonder are mentioned first for the Qur’an?
questions.answer: Seven kinds.

questions.question: What other number is given to show its miraculous nature?
questions.answer: Forty aspects.

questions.question: What does the passage say about proving these things?
questions.answer: It says strong proofs were given in another treatise.

questions.question: What does the traveller choose to do instead of giving all the proofs here?
questions.answer: He keeps speaking and shares his conclusion.

questions.question: What is his conclusion about the messenger?
questions.answer: The messenger would never lie.

questions.question: Why does the traveller think lying is impossible here?
questions.answer: Because it would break trust with Allah’s message.

questions.question: What is one big reason the passage gives for trusting the messenger?
questions.answer: He brings the Qur’an from Allah.

questions.question: What does the passage say people have done with the Qur’an in each century?
questions.answer: They have accepted and affirmed it.

questions.question: What do the large number of followers help show in this passage?
questions.answer: They help show the message is widely believed.

questions.question: What do the seven ways and forty aspects tell us about the Qur’an?
questions.answer: They show it is full of miracles.

questions.question: Why are the details not all explained in this short passage?
questions.answer: They are left to a different book.

questions.question: What two roles of the messenger are named near the end?
questions.answer: He carries the message and proclaims it.

questions.question: What would lying do to the decree he carries?
questions.answer: It would go against it.

questions.question: What would lying do to his duty to Allah?
questions.answer: It would be disloyal to Allah.

questions.question: What lesson should a student learn from this passage?
questions.answer: Allah’s message is true, and His messenger is truthful.

questions.question: What is the passage mainly talking about: a battle, a journey, or a divine message?
questions.answer: A divine message.

questions.question: What is the divine message named in the passage?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: From whom does this message come?
questions.answer: It comes from the Lord of the universe.

questions.question: What does the passage say many people do with this message over many centuries?
questions.answer: They accept and confirm it.

questions.question: How does the passage show that the Qur’an is amazing?
questions.answer: It says it has several wondrous ways and many miraculous aspects.

questions.question: Where are the fuller proofs said to be found?
questions.answer: In the Twenty-Fifth Word.

questions.question: Why might the traveller skip the long explanation here?
questions.answer: Because it has already been explained well somewhere else.

questions.question: What does “conveyor and proclaimer” mean here?
questions.answer: Someone who brings the message and tells it to people.

questions.question: Why can such a person not be dishonest?
questions.answer: Because dishonesty would betray Allah’s message.

questions.question: What final thought does the traveller give about the messenger?
questions.answer: He cannot possibly be a liar.

questions.question: What does the messenger hold in his hand in the passage?
questions.answer: A decree.

questions.question: Is this decree from people or from Allah?
questions.answer: It is from Allah.

questions.question: What is the name of this decree?
questions.answer: The Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the passage say people in every century do about it?
questions.answer: They accept it and stand by it.

questions.question: About how many people are mentioned?
questions.answer: More than 300 million.

questions.question: What two numbers are used to show how miraculous the Qur’an is?
questions.answer: Seven and forty.

questions.question: What is said about the treatise called the Twenty-Fifth Word?
questions.answer: It gives detailed and strong proofs about the Qur’an.

questions.question: What does the speaker decide after mentioning that treatise?
questions.answer: To leave those details there and continue.

questions.question: What wrong actions are impossible for the messenger, according to the passage?
questions.answer: Lying and betrayal.

questions.question: Why are those wrong actions impossible for him?
questions.answer: Because he is delivering Allah’s decree faithfully.
